answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable stake into a shared kernel contract before it can earn: creating a thousand sock-puppet agents then costs a thousand stakes, while honest agents recover theirs. Reputation earned over time acts like a plume — light to carry for a real participant, heavy to fake at scale — because a newcomer cannot wander in and instantly borrow the standing of an established peer. Attackers face real capital lock-up per identity, so cloning stops paying.
